raw_texts_per_turn:
Below is a 12-week, progressive couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old with exercise-induced asthma (EIA), controlled on a SABA inhaler. It emphasizes thorough warm-ups, careful exposure to cold air, and gradual intensity. The goal is to comfortably complete a 5K by Week 12.

Key safety and management notes for EIA
- Pre-exercise: Follow GP guidance on SABA use (if prescribed as pre-exercise). Ensure inhaler is accessible at all times.
- Warm-up priority: Always include a gradual, extended warm-up (10–15 minutes) with dynamic mobility and easy ramp-up. Many with EIA benefit from a “refractory period” after an initial light bout; this plan integrates a progressive warm-up.
- Cold air considerations: If possible, train indoors or in milder conditions on very cold days; otherwise, use a face covering/buff to warm/humidify air, start extra gently, and avoid peak intensity in the cold.
- Symptom monitoring: Stop/reduce intensity if coughing, chest tightness, unusual wheeze, or disproportionate breathlessness occurs. Resume only when symptoms settle. Log any triggers.
- Recovery: Prioritize nasal breathing early in warm-up if comfortable; shift to relaxed oral/nasal mix as intensity rises. Cool down thoroughly.

Structure and frequency
- Weekly frequency: 3 run-walk sessions (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat) with at least 1 day between.
- Cross-training: 1–2 optional low-impact aerobic sessions (cycling, elliptical, brisk walk, swim in warm/humid environment) on non-run days.
- Strength: 2 short sessions/week focused on lower body, core, and postural strength (20–25 min).
- Progression: Conservative, with repeatable weeks if symptoms or fatigue warrant.

Universal session template (each run day)
1) Pre-run checklist (2–3 min): 
   - Confirm inhaler on person, check weather, use buff in cold, note allergens/pollution.
2) Extended warm-up (10–15 min total):
   - 5 min easy walk, nasal if comfortable.
   - 3–5 min dynamic mobility: ankle circles, leg swings, hip openers, thoracic rotations.
   - 2–5 min easy jog or brisk walk-jog blend, finishing at RPE 3–4/10.
3) Main set: Run/walk intervals per week plan at RPE 4–6. Keep first interval easier.
4) Cool-down (8–10 min): 5–7 min easy walk until breathing normalizes; gentle calves/hips stretches.
5) Post-run note (1–2 min): Log symptoms, perceived exertion, environment, and any need to modify next session.

Intensity guide
- Use RPE scale 1–10. Most work at RPE 4–6; avoid >7 in cold or early phases.
- Breathing: Aim for conversational pace on run segments.

Strength sessions (2x/week, non-consecutive)
- Session A:
  - Bodyweight squat or goblet squat 3x8–10
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust 3x10–12
  - Step-up (low box) 3x8/side
  - Dead bug 3x6/side
  - Side plank 2x20–30s/side
- Session B:
  - Romanian deadlift (DB/KB) 3x8–10
  - Reverse lunge 3x8/side
  - Calf raise 3x12–15
  - Bird dog 3x8/side
  - Pallof press 3x8–10/side
- Rest 60–90s. Start light; focus on control and nasal breathing where possible.

Optional cross-training (1–2x/week, 20–30 min, RPE 3–5): cycling, elliptical, indoor track, or pool in warm air; avoid cold outdoor high-intensity efforts.

Weekly plan (3 run days/week)

Week 1 – Build habit, gentle exposure
- Goal: Comfortable walk-jog with zero symptom flare.
- Main set: 8 x 1 min run / 90 sec walk (total ~20 min), RPE 4–5.
- Total session time: ~40–45 min including warm-up/cool-down.
- Strength: 2 sessions (light).
- Notes: If cold, add 3–5 min extra warm-up walking and use a buff.

Week 2 – Slight volume increase
- Main set: 6 x 90 sec run / 2 min walk (total ~21 min), RPE 4–5.
- Keep first 1–2 intervals easier (RPE 4).
- Strength: progress 1–2 reps if form solid.

Week 3 – Longer run segments
- Main set: 5 x 2 min run / 2 min walk (total ~20 min), RPE 4–5.
- Optional 1 easy cross-training session.

Week 4 – Consolidate, introduce 3-min runs
- Main set: 4 x 3 min run / 2 min walk (total ~20 min), RPE 4–5.
- If any EIA symptoms in prior week, repeat Week 3 before advancing.

Week 5 – Extend continuous time
- Main set: 3 min run / 90 sec walk, then 5 min run / 2 min walk, repeat once (total run time 16 min; total set ~24 min).
- RPE 4–5; avoid surges, especially in cold or wind.

Week 6 – Steady progress
- Main set: 3 x 8 min run / 3 min walk (total run 24 min).
- Aim for very steady, conversational pace. If symptoms, reduce to 3 x 6 min run / 3 min walk.

Week 7 – Threshold to continuous running
- Main set: 2 x 12 min run / 3 min walk (total run 24 min).
- Maintain RPE 4–5. If finish feeling strong, add an easy 2–3 min jog before cool-down.

Week 8 – First continuous run block
- Main set: 18–20 min continuous easy run.
- If symptoms: split into 2 x 10 min run / 2–3 min walk.

- The next day: 20–30 min very easy walk or spin; mobility.
- Training resume: If planning beyond 5K, take 2–3 easy days before re‑introducing quality.

Micro‑adjustments for freshness
- If legs feel heavy by midweek: cut Wednesday primer volume by 25–30% and skip Friday strides.
- If he had a tough week or poor sleep: make Friday a walk only.

This finisher week balances sharpness with safety, giving him clear routines and confidence for a strong, symptom‑free 5K.

Here’s the complete 12-week Couch-to-5K program with all adjustments integrated: extended warm-ups for exercise-induced asthma, strength twice weekly, intervals (Weeks 6–12), tempo on alternating weeks from Week 8, a Week 8 parkrun test (controlled), pace progression in later weeks, and a finisher/race-week structure. Three run days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat). Strength Tue/Fri. Optional cross-training 1–2x on non-run days. Always carry SABA inhaler, warm up thoroughly, and favor indoor/treadmill or a buff in cold/dry air.

Global session template for run days
- Pre-run checklist (2–3 min): Inhaler on person; check weather/allergens; choose indoor if cold/dry; wear buff outdoors in cold.
- Extended warm-up (10–15 min):
  - 5 min easy walk → brisk walk/jog (nasal if comfortable)
  - 3–5 min dynamic mobility (ankles, hips, T-spine)
  - 2–5 min easy jog blend; add 2–3 x 20–30 sec gentle pick-ups only for tempo/interval days in warm, symptom-free conditions
- Cool-down (8–10 min): 5–7 min easy walk/jog until breathing normalizes; gentle calf/hip stretches.
- Intensity anchors: E (RPE 3–4), S (RPE 4–5), T tempo (RPE 6), I intervals (RPE 6–7 but controlled), Strides ST 10–15 sec smooth, full recovery, only in warm/symptom-free conditions.

Strength training (Tue & Fri, 20–30 min, non-consecutive, light-moderate breathing load)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation)
  - Session A: Goblet or box squat 3x8–10; Glute bridge 3x10–12 (2-sec squeeze); Step-up 3x8/side; Dead bug 3x6–8/side; Side plank 2x20–30s/side
  - Session B: DB/KB RDL 3x8–10; Reverse lunge 3x8/side; Calf raise 3x12–15; Bird dog 3x8/side (2-sec pause); Pallof press 3x8–10/side
- Weeks 5–8 (Strength endurance/single-leg)
  - Session A: Goblet squat 4x8; Hip thrust 3x10–12; Step-down (3-sec lower) 3x8/side; Dead bug heel taps 3x8–10/side; Side plank + abduction 2x20–30s/side
  - Session B: DB/KB RDL 4x8; Split squat 3x8–10/side; Calf raise 4x12–15; Cable/band row 3x10–12; Pallof press 3x10–12/side
- Weeks 9–12 (Run-specific strength/control)
  - Session A: Front-foot elevated split squat 4x6–8/side; Hip thrust 4x8–10; Single-leg RDL 3x8/side; Marching calf raise 3x12/side; Dead bug or hollow hold 3x20–30s
  - Session B: Box/goblet squat 4x6–8; Lateral lunge 3x8/side; Hamstring slide-outs 3x6–8; Half-kneeling 1-arm row 3x10/side; Pallof press iso 3x20–30s/side
- Notes: Rest 60–90s; leave 2–3 reps in reserve; avoid breath-holding. If legs feel heavy, drop 1 set from lower-body lifts that week. Weeks 12 keep strength very light (activation only).

Optional cross-training (1–2x/week, 20–30 min, RPE 3–5): bike, elliptical, brisk walk, or pool in warm air.

Week-by-week running plan

Week 1 – Gentle start, zero flare
- Run 1–3 (3x/week):
  - Main: 8 x 1 min run / 90 sec walk (RPE 4–5). Total set ~20 min.
  - Total session ~40–45 min with warm-up/cool-down.
- Strength: 2 sessions (light).
- Notes: Add 3–5 min extra warm-up if cold; use buff.

Week 2 – Small volume increase
- Runs:
  - Main: 6 x 90 sec run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5) per session.
- Strength: Progress reps slightly if form solid.

Week 3 – Longer run bouts
- Runs:
  - Main: 5 x 2 min run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5).
- Optional 1 easy cross-train session.

Week 4 – Consolidate, 3-min runs
- Runs:
  - Main: 4 x 3 min run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5).
- If any EIA symptoms last week, repeat Week 3.

Week 5 – Extend time, steady pacing
- Runs:
  - Main: 3 min run / 90 sec walk, then 5 min run / 2 min walk, repeat once (total run 16 min; set ~24 min), RPE 4–5.
- Strength: Maintain; avoid pushing to failure.

Week 6 – Intro intervals begin
- Run 1 (Easy): 20–22 min continuous E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 6 x 1 min I (RPE 6–7, controlled) / 2 min E jog-walk.
- Run 3 (Long E): 24–26 min continuous E.
- Strength: Normal. Prefer indoor for intervals if cold/dry.

Week 7 – Intervals progress
- Run 1 (Easy): 22–24 min E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 5 x 90 sec I / 2 min E. Cold/windy alt: 6 x 60 sec I / 2 min E.
- Run 3 (Long E): 24–26 min E.
- Strength: Steady. Keep breathing relaxed during sets.

Week 8 – First tempo week + Parkrun (controlled test)
- Weekly layout example: Mon Easy, Wed Light pace change, Sat Parkrun test.
- Run 1 (Tempo intro): 2 x 8 min T (RPE ~6) with 3 min E jog between. Cold/dry alt: 2 x 8 min S or 16–18 min S.
- Run 2 (Light pace change OR Easy): 10 min E + 4 x 60 sec S (90 sec E) + 5 min E. If legs heavy, make it pure E for 18–20 min.
- Run 3 (Parkrun test, controlled 5K):
  - Warm-up 12–15 min as per template.
  - Pacing: Km1 upper-E→S; Km2–3 S; Km4 S→low‑T only if stable; Km5 hold RPE 5–6. Not a max effort.
  - Cool-down 8–10 min.
- Strength: Keep both sessions light-moderate this week.

Week 9 – Back to intervals, build continuous easy
- Run 1 (Easy): 22–24 min E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 5 x 2 min I / 2 min E.
- Run 3 (Long E): 22–24 min continuous E (or 2 x 10–12 min with 2–3 min walk if needed).
- Optional strides: After Run 1, 3–4 x 10–15 sec only if warm/symptom-free.

Week 10 – Tempo build + steady long
- Run 1 (Tempo build): 3 x 8 min T (2–3 min E). Stop at 2 reps if RPE creeps >6. Cold/dry alt: 3 x 6 min S.
- Run 2 (Easy): 26–28 min E.
- Run 3 (Strides session): 12–15 min E + 6 x 20 sec ST (full walk recovery) + 6–8 min E. Skip ST if cold/symptoms.
- Strength: Keep volume steady; drop 1 lower-body set if legs heavy.

Week 11 – Quality choice (tempo or intervals) + near-goal long run
- Run 1 (Coach’s choice based on feel/weather):
  - Option A Tempo: 2 x 10 min T (3 min E).
  - Option B Intervals: 2 x (3 min I + 2 min E) + 3 x (2 min I + 90 sec E).
- Run 2 (Easy): 30–32 min E.
- Run 3 (Steady feel + optional strides): 10–12 min E + 8–10 min S continuous + 5–8 min E. Optional 3 x 15 sec ST if very fresh/warm.
- Strength: Maintain; avoid failure.

Week 12 – Finisher / race-week (taper + race)
- Mon (Easy + optional strides): 18–20 min E; optional 3 x 12–15 sec ST (skip if cold/symptoms).
- Tue (Light strength activation, 20–25 min): 2 rounds—light squats 2x8, bridges 2x10, split squats 2x6/side, light rows 2x10, dead bug 2x6/side, side plank 2x20s/side. Easy mobility and breathing.
- Wed (Race primer—choose one):
  - Option A Short tempo: 2 x 6–8 min low‑T (RPE ~6) with 3 min E. Cold/dry alt: 2 x 6–8 min S.
  - Option B Short intervals: 6 x 60–75 sec I (RPE 6–7) / 90 sec E. Indoors preferred if cold.
- Thu: Rest or 20–25 min relaxed walk + mobility.
- Fri (Shakeout): 12–15 min E; optional 2 x 10–12 sec very light ST; skip if cold/symptoms.
- Sat/Sun (5K race):
  - Warm-up 15–18 min (walk→jog, mobility, 2–3 gentle pick-ups; skip pick-ups if cold).
  - Pacing: Km1 upper‑E→S; Km2–3 S; Km4 S→low‑T if stable; Km5 hold RPE 5–6. Aim negative split. Downshift/walk if symptoms.
  - Cool-down 10–12 min easy walk/jog.
- Post-race: Carb + 20–30 g protein within 60 min; hydrate; easy walk/spin next day 20–30 min.

Asthma-specific safeguards (apply every week)
- Prioritize extended warm-ups and indoor options in cold/dry weather; wear a buff outdoors.
- Avoid sudden surges; cap RPE at 6 for tempo/intervals, 7 max on short I reps when warm and symptom-free.
- If cough/wheeze/tightness or unusual breathlessness appears: downshift to E or walk immediately; extend recovery; stop if not resolving; log triggers. Repeat prior successful week before progressing.
- Illness or high allergen/pollution: reduce to easy running or cross-train indoors; resume progression after two symptom-free sessions.

Pacing guidance after the Week 8 parkrun test
- Use parkrun average pace as reference:
  - Easy (E): ~60–75 sec/km slower
  - Steady (S): ~30–45 sec/km slower
  - Tempo (T): ~10–25 sec/km slower (only in warm/safe conditions)
- Strides: Technique-only, smooth and short, full recovery.

Recovery and nutrition basics
- Sleep 7–9 hours; hydrate to pale yellow urine.
- Pre-run 60–90 min: small carb snack if needed (banana, toast + honey, yogurt).
- Post-run: Balanced meal with 20–30 g protein + carbs; electrolytes if warm/indoors.
- Cool-down thoroughly; avoid abrupt stops.

This integrated plan builds him from couch to a confident 5K, safely incorporates intervals and tempo, leverages a Week 8 parkrun as a pacing rehearsal, and finishes with a race-ready taper while honoring exercise-induced asthma precautions.

Here’s the complete 12-week Couch-to-5K program with all adjustments integrated: extended warm-ups for exercise-induced asthma, strength twice weekly, intervals (Weeks 6–12), tempo on alternating weeks from Week 8, a Week 8 parkrun test (controlled), pace progression in later weeks, and a finisher/race-week structure. Three run days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat). Strength Tue/Fri. Optional cross-training 1–2x on non-run days. Always carry SABA inhaler, warm up thoroughly, and favor indoor/treadmill or a buff in cold/dry air.

Global session template for run days
- Pre-run checklist (2–3 min): Inhaler on person; check weather/allergens; choose indoor if cold/dry; wear buff outdoors in cold.
- Extended warm-up (10–15 min):
  - 5 min easy walk → brisk walk/jog (nasal if comfortable)
  - 3–5 min dynamic mobility (ankles, hips, T-spine)
  - 2–5 min easy jog blend; add 2–3 x 20–30 sec gentle pick-ups only for tempo/interval days in warm, symptom-free conditions
- Cool-down (8–10 min): 5–7 min easy walk/jog until breathing normalizes; gentle calf/hip stretches.
- Intensity anchors: E (RPE 3–4), S (RPE 4–5), T tempo (RPE 6), I intervals (RPE 6–7 but controlled), Strides ST 10–15 sec smooth, full recovery, only in warm/symptom-free conditions.

Strength training (Tue & Fri, 20–30 min, non-consecutive, light-moderate breathing load)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation)
  - Session A: Goblet or box squat 3x8–10; Glute bridge 3x10–12 (2-sec squeeze); Step-up 3x8/side; Dead bug 3x6–8/side; Side plank 2x20–30s/side
  - Session B: DB/KB RDL 3x8–10; Reverse lunge 3x8/side; Calf raise 3x12–15; Bird dog 3x8/side (2-sec pause); Pallof press 3x8–10/side
- Weeks 5–8 (Strength endurance/single-leg)
  - Session A: Goblet squat 4x8; Hip thrust 3x10–12; Step-down (3-sec lower) 3x8/side; Dead bug heel taps 3x8–10/side; Side plank + abduction 2x20–30s/side
  - Session B: DB/KB RDL 4x8; Split squat 3x8–10/side; Calf raise 4x12–15; Cable/band row 3x10–12; Pallof press 3x10–12/side
- Weeks 9–12 (Run-specific strength/control)
  - Session A: Front-foot elevated split squat 4x6–8/side; Hip thrust 4x8–10; Single-leg RDL 3x8/side; Marching calf raise 3x12/side; Dead bug or hollow hold 3x20–30s
  - Session B: Box/goblet squat 4x6–8; Lateral lunge 3x8/side; Hamstring slide-outs 3x6–8; Half-kneeling 1-arm row 3x10/side; Pallof press iso 3x20–30s/side
- Notes: Rest 60–90s; leave 2–3 reps in reserve; avoid breath-holding. If legs feel heavy, drop 1 set from lower-body lifts that week. Weeks 12 keep strength very light (activation only).

Optional cross-training (1–2x/week, 20–30 min, RPE 3–5): bike, elliptical, brisk walk, or pool in warm air.

Week-by-week running plan

Week 1 – Gentle start, zero flare
- Run 1–3 (3x/week):
  - Main: 8 x 1 min run / 90 sec walk (RPE 4–5). Total set ~20 min.
  - Total session ~40–45 min with warm-up/cool-down.
- Strength: 2 sessions (light).
- Notes: Add 3–5 min extra warm-up if cold; use buff.

Week 2 – Small volume increase
- Runs:
  - Main: 6 x 90 sec run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5) per session.
- Strength: Progress reps slightly if form solid.

Week 3 – Longer run bouts
- Runs:
  - Main: 5 x 2 min run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5).
- Optional 1 easy cross-train session.

Week 4 – Consolidate, 3-min runs
- Runs:
  - Main: 4 x 3 min run / 2 min walk (RPE 4–5).
- If any EIA symptoms last week, repeat Week 3.

Week 5 – Extend time, steady pacing
- Runs:
  - Main: 3 min run / 90 sec walk, then 5 min run / 2 min walk, repeat once (total run 16 min; set ~24 min), RPE 4–5.
- Strength: Maintain; avoid pushing to failure.

Week 6 – Intro intervals begin
- Run 1 (Easy): 20–22 min continuous E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 6 x 1 min I (RPE 6–7, controlled) / 2 min E jog-walk.
- Run 3 (Long E): 24–26 min continuous E.
- Strength: Normal. Prefer indoor for intervals if cold/dry.

Week 7 – Intervals progress
- Run 1 (Easy): 22–24 min E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 5 x 90 sec I / 2 min E. Cold/windy alt: 6 x 60 sec I / 2 min E.
- Run 3 (Long E): 24–26 min E.
- Strength: Steady. Keep breathing relaxed during sets.

Week 8 – First tempo week + Parkrun (controlled test)
- Weekly layout example: Mon Easy, Wed Light pace change, Sat Parkrun test.
- Run 1 (Tempo intro): 2 x 8 min T (RPE ~6) with 3 min E jog between. Cold/dry alt: 2 x 8 min S or 16–18 min S.
- Run 2 (Light pace change OR Easy): 10 min E + 4 x 60 sec S (90 sec E) + 5 min E. If legs heavy, make it pure E for 18–20 min.
- Run 3 (Parkrun test, controlled 5K):
  - Warm-up 12–15 min as per template.
  - Pacing: Km1 upper-E→S; Km2–3 S; Km4 S→low‑T only if stable; Km5 hold RPE 5–6. Not a max effort.
  - Cool-down 8–10 min.
- Strength: Keep both sessions light-moderate this week.

Week 9 – Back to intervals, build continuous easy
- Run 1 (Easy): 22–24 min E.
- Run 2 (Intervals): 5 x 2 min I / 2 min E.
- Run 3 (Long E): 22–24 min continuous E (or 2 x 10–12 min with 2–3 min walk if needed).

Week 10 – Tempo build + steady long
- Run 1 (Tempo build): 3 x 8 min T (2–3 min E). Stop at 2 reps if RPE creeps >6. Cold/dry alt: 3 x 6 min S.
- Run 2 (Easy): 26–28 min E.
- Run 3 (Strides session): 12–15 min E + 6 x 20 sec ST (full walk recovery) + 6–8 min E. Skip ST if cold/symptoms.
- Strength: Keep volume steady; drop 1 lower-body set if legs heavy.

Week 11 – Quality choice (tempo or intervals) + near-goal long run
- Run 1 (Coach’s choice based on feel/weather):
  - Option A Tempo: 2 x 10 min T (3 min E).
  - Option B Intervals: 2 x (3 min I + 2 min E) + 3 x (2 min I + 90 sec E).
- Run 2 (Easy): 30–32 min E.

Week 12 – Finisher / race-week (taper + race)
- Mon (Easy + optional strides): 18–20 min E; optional 3 x 12–15 sec ST (skip if cold/symptoms).
- Tue (Light strength activation, 20–25 min): 2 rounds—light squats 2x8, bridges 2x10, split squats 2x6/side, light rows 2x10, dead bug 2x6/side, side plank 2x20s/side. Easy mobility and breathing.
- Wed (Race primer—choose one):
  - Option A Short tempo: 2 x 6–8 min low‑T (RPE ~6) with 3 min E. Cold/dry alt: 2 x 6–8 min S.
  - Option B Short intervals: 6 x 60–75 sec I (RPE 6–7) / 90 sec E. Indoors preferred if cold.
- Thu: Rest or 20–25 min relaxed walk + mobility.
- Fri (Shakeout): 12–15 min E; optional 2 x 10–12 sec very light ST; skip if cold/symptoms.
- Sat/Sun (5K race):
  - Warm-up 15–18 min (walk→jog, mobility, 2–3 gentle pick-ups; skip pick-ups if cold).
  - Pacing: Km1 upper‑E→S; Km2–3 S; Km4 S→low‑T if stable; Km5 hold RPE 5–6. Aim negative split. Downshift/walk if symptoms.
  - Cool-down 10–12 min easy walk/jog.
- Post-race: Carb + 20–30 g protein within 60 min; hydrate; easy walk/spin next day 20–30 min.

Asthma-specific safeguards (apply every week)
- Prioritize extended warm-ups and indoor options in cold/dry weather; wear a buff outdoors.
- Avoid sudden surges; cap RPE at 6 for tempo/intervals, 7 max on short I reps when warm and symptom-free.
- If cough/wheeze/tightness or unusual breathlessness appears: downshift to E or walk immediately; extend recovery; stop if not resolving; log triggers. Repeat prior successful week before progressing.
- Illness or high allergen/pollution: reduce to easy running or cross-train indoors; resume progression after two symptom-free sessions.

Pacing guidance after the Week 8 parkrun test
- Use parkrun average pace as reference:
  - Easy (E): ~60–75 sec/km slower
  - Steady (S): ~30–45 sec/km slower
  - Tempo (T): ~10–25 sec/km slower (only in warm/safe conditions)
- Strides: Technique-only, smooth and short, full recovery.

Recovery and nutrition basics
- Sleep 7–9 hours; hydrate to pale yellow urine.
- Pre-run 60–90 min: small carb snack if needed (banana, toast + honey, yogurt).
- Post-run: Balanced meal with 20–30 g protein + carbs; electrolytes if warm/indoors.
- Cool-down thoroughly; avoid abrupt stops.
